5	//
6	// Implements DESIGN-TC-PIPELINE.md §4.1 item 1 + item 2: the in-kernel
7	// `wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned.m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16` warp-group MMA with
8	// smem-resident A AND B operands ("ss" = shared-shared), the 64-bit smem

10	// fragment management, swizzle-mode handling, and the
11	// wgmma.fence / wgmma.commit_group / wgmma.wait_group choreography.
12	//
13	// This is the hand-written, correctness-gated GEMM-engine layer the three
14	// model-stage headers (decoder / vit / mamba3) build their tiled fwd/bwd
15	// pipelines on (DESIGN §3). It does NOT include or depend on CUTLASS
16	// (mma.cuh): host-launched CUTLASS collectives are not device-callable and
17	// are explicitly REJECTED for the L3 persistent-megakernel path
18	// (DESIGN Appendix B). This header is the only WGMMA path inside the kernel.
19	//
20	// PORTABILITY (COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md rules 1-4): header-only, self-contained,
21	// substrate + CUDA only. It includes ONLY <cuda_bf16.h> / <cuda_runtime.h> /
22	// <cstdint>; a third project lifts THIS file (+ warp_specialize.cuh /
23	// primitives.cuh for the pipeline) and instantiates the wrappers with no other
24	// repo dependency. All arch-specific PTX is guarded on __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900;
25	// pre-sm_90 / gfx942 compile to the documented scalar fallback so the codegen
26	// matrix still builds (the model headers keep their scalar `*_linear` there).
27	//
28	// MAXIMAL-PTX DISCIPLINE: every inline-asm sequence cites the PTX ISA section
29	// (CUDA 12.4 / PTX ISA 8.4) it implements. The PTX is the point.
30	//
31	// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
32	//  API CONTRACT — what a model-stage header author calls (integration seam)
33	// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
34	//
35	// The next phase (R2.3, wiring wgmma into model_stage_{decoder,vit,mamba3})
36	// consumes EXACTLY the following. All symbols live in `sg::sm90::wgs::`
37	// (the same namespace as warp_specialize.cuh's Mbarrier / setmaxnreg helpers —
38	// this header REOPENS that namespace, it does not fork a new one).
39	//
40	// --- 1. The accumulator fragment ------------------------------------------
41	//   template <int N> struct WgmmaAccum;
42	//     Per-thread fp32 accumulator for an m64×N output tile. Holds N/2 floats
43	//     in registers (NOT smem). One object per consumer thread; the 128
44	//     warpgroup threads together hold the full 64×N tile. Layout is the
45	//     PTX ISA "Figure 149 / register fragment for .f32 accumulators"
46	//     (§<ip>.3) mapping — see frag_row()/frag_col() below for the exact
47	//     thread→(row,col) decode the epilogue uses to store results.
48	//       .zero()                 — clear all N/2 lanes to 0.0f (call before the
49	//                                 first accumulating wgmma if scaleD=accumulate).
50	//       .c[i]                   — the i-th fp32 register (i in [0, N/2)).
51	//
52	// --- 2. The smem matrix descriptor ----------------------------------------
53	//   struct SmemDesc { uint64_t desc; };
54	//   __device__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc<Swizzle>(const void* smem_base,
55	//                                                uint32_t lbo, uint32_t sbo);
56	//     Packs the 64-bit shared-memory descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4,
57	//     "Shared memory matrix descriptor"). `smem_base` is a generic smem
58	//     pointer to the (0,0) element of the operand's core-matrix tile; lbo /
59	//     sbo are the leading- / stride-byte-offsets in BYTES (the helper applies

65	//       make_desc_B_kmajor<N,    Swizzle>(smem)  — B operand (N rows × K=16)
66	//
67	// --- 3. The MMA + choreography --------------------------------------------
68	//   __device__ void wgmma_fence();                         // §<ip>.2
69	//   __device__ void wgmma_commit_group();                  // §<ip>.5
70	//   template <int N> __device__ void wgmma_wait_group();   // §<ip>.6
71	//
72	//   template <int N, int ScaleD, int TransA, int TransB>
73	//   __device__ void wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16(WgmmaAccum<N>& acc,
74	//                                       SmemDesc descA, SmemDesc descB);
75	//     One m64×N×16 ss-wgmma issue (PTX ISA §<ip>.1). ScaleD=0 OVERWRITES
76	//     the accumulator (D = A·B); ScaleD=1 ACCUMULATES (D += A·B). TransA/TransB
77	//     select operand transpose (the .trans descriptor bit). N must be one of
78	//     the legal bf16 shapes {8,16,32,64,96,128,256}; the design selects 128
79	//     (in/out/ff GEMMs), 96 (decoder head V=99 padded), 64 (ragged).
80	//
81	//   Full mainloop helper (the choreography in one call — what the model
82	//   headers actually invoke for a K-tile chain):
83	//   template <int N, int TransA, int TransB, typename DescGen>
84	//   __device__ void wgmma_mainloop_kchain(WgmmaAccum<N>& acc, int k_steps,
85	//                                         DescGen gen);
86	//     Runs `k_steps` ss-wgmma issues in FIXED ASCENDING k-order (DESIGN §3.1
87	//     determinism rule), first issue ScaleD=0 then accumulate, with one
88	//     fence before the group and one commit+wait_group<0> after. `gen(k)`
89	//     returns the {descA, descB} pair for k-step k (the caller advances the
90	//     smem pointer / pipeline stage). Bit-identical regardless of how the
91	//     caller stages the operands (cp.async vs pre-loaded), which is what gate
92	//     (c) (pipelined == unpipelined) verifies.
93	//
94	// --- 4. Tunable template parameters (DESIGN §9, SG_TUNED_* names) ----------
95	//   SG_TUNED_TILE_N   — wgmma N (output tile width). Default 128. {64,128,256}.
96	//                       The `N` template arg above is bound to this by callers.
97	//   SG_TUNED_TILE_M   — token-tile rows per CTA (the M-tile). Default 128.
98	//                       wgmma M is fixed at 64 (the atom); TILE_M/64 = number
99	//                       of stacked atoms a CTA's consumer warpgroup issues.
100	//   (SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH / SG_TUNED_WG_COUNT belong to tile_pipeline.cuh.)
101	//   Absent definitions yield a correct untuned wrapper (CONTRACT rule 3).
102	//
103	// --- 5. smem layout + alignment requirements (cite: PTX ISA) --------------
104	//   * Operand smem tiles MUST be 16-byte aligned. The matrix descriptor's
105	//     start-address field is the smem byte address >>4 (PTX ISA §<ip>.4),
106	//     so the low 4 bits MUST be zero — a non-16B-aligned tile silently drops
107	//     them and reads the wrong matrix. Allocate operand smem as
108	//     `__align__(16)` (or via an aligned smem arena).
109	//   * The wgmma is `.aligned`: ALL 128 threads of the warpgroup must execute

112	//     multiple of 128 and the issuing warpgroup must be convergent.
113	//   * The fp32 accumulators written by a NON-wgmma instruction (e.g. .zero())

115	//     issue (PTX ISA §<ip>.2 wgmma.fence). Reading the accumulators in
116	//     the epilogue must follow wgmma_wait_group<0>() (§<ip>.6).
117	//   * Core-matrix granularity: bf16 operands are consumed as 8×16-element
118	//     (rows×cols, "8 rows of 16 cols", 128-bit) core matrices; the K-tile is
119	//     16 (the atom's k). The B (RHS) tile for an N-wide output is N×16 bf16.

146	//  Swizzle mode (PTX ISA §<ip>.4, descriptor bits 62-61 "swizzle mode").
147	//
148	//  The shared-memory matrix descriptor encodes how the 128-bit core-matrix
149	//  rows are interleaved in smem to avoid bank conflicts on the wgmma read.
150	//  CRITICAL: the descriptor's layout_type field (bits 63:62) does NOT use a
151	//  size-ascending encoding. The hardware/CUTLASS encoding is
152	//  (cute/arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp LayoutType, verified):
153	//    NONE/INTERLEAVE = 0,  SWIZZLE_128B = 1,  SWIZZLE_64B = 2,  SWIZZLE_32B = 3.
154	//  (An earlier draft had 32B=1/128B=3 swapped; the correctness path uses NONE=0
155	//  so it was unaffected, but the perf-phase swizzle modes MUST use these values.)
156	//
157	//  CORRECTNESS-PATH NOTE (deviation flagged in the report): the gated /
158	//  tested numerics path ships swizzle = NONE (kSwizzleNone). NONE is a
159	//  fully-legal descriptor mode (§<ip>.4) and is the layout the
160	//  correctness gates validate against torch. The 128B-swizzle layout is a
161	//  PERF-PHASE optimization (bank-conflict elimination on the smem read) and
162	//  is exposed here as the template parameter the model headers will select
163	//  once the quiet-GPU perf phase measures it; it is NOT required for any
164	//  correctness gate. See DESIGN §4.1 ("specify the 128-byte-swizzle layout"
165	//  is the perf target; phase-1 staging uses cp.async, §4.1 item 3).
166	// =========================================================================
167	enum SwizzleMode : uint32_t {
168	    kSwizzleNone = 0,   // INTERLEAVE / no swizzle (the correctness-path layout)
169	    kSwizzle128B = 1,   // SWIZZLE_128B
170	    kSwizzle64B  = 2,   // SWIZZLE_64B
171	    kSwizzle32B  = 3,   // SWIZZLE_32B
172	};

174	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	//  generic-smem-pointer → matrix-descriptor start address.
176	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.4: the descriptor's bits 13-0 hold the start address of
177	//  the matrix in shared memory, encoded as the 18-bit smem byte address with
178	//  the low 4 bits dropped — i.e. addr_field = (smem_byte_addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4.
179	//  The low 4 bits MUST be zero (16-byte alignment) or they are silently lost.
180	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_desc_encode_addr(const void* smem_ptr) {
182	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
183	    uint32_t a = static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(smem_ptr));
184	    return (a & 0x3FFFFu) >> 4;
185	#else
186	    (void)smem_ptr;
187	    return 0u;
188	#endif
189	}

191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4).
193	//
194	//  64-bit layout (bit ranges per the ISA table):
195	//    bits  13: 0  start address (smem byte addr >> 4)
196	//    bits  15:14  (reserved / 0)
197	//    bits  29:16  leading-dimension byte offset (LBO) >> 4
198	//    bits  31:30  (reserved / 0)
199	//    bits  45:32  stride-dimension byte offset (SBO) >> 4
200	//    bits  48:46  (reserved / 0)
201	//    bits  51:49  matrix base offset (for swizzle; 0 for our tiles)
202	//    bits  61:52  (reserved / 0)
203	//    bits  63:62  swizzle / layout mode (0 none / 1 128B / 2 64B / 3 32B —
204	//                 the CUTLASS LayoutType encoding, see SwizzleMode above)
205	//
206	//  LBO and SBO are the byte offsets between consecutive "core matrices" along
207	//  the leading and stride dimensions respectively (§<ip>.3 "Strides").
208	//  Both are encoded >>4 (16-byte granular). The exact (LBO,SBO) depend on the
209	//  operand's smem tile layout; the make_desc_*_kmajor builders below compute
210	//  them for the canonical row-major-K bf16 tiles the model headers stage.
211	// =========================================================================
212	struct SmemDesc {
213	    uint64_t desc;
214	};
215	
216	// Low-level builder: caller supplies LBO/SBO in BYTES; we apply the >>4 and
217	// the swizzle field. Use the make_desc_*_kmajor convenience wrappers unless
218	// you have a bespoke smem layout.
219	template <SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
220	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc(
221	    const void* smem_base, uint32_t lbo_bytes, uint32_t sbo_bytes,
222	    uint32_t base_offset = 0u
223	) {
224	    SmemDesc d;
225	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
226	    uint64_t addr = static_cast<uint64_t>(smem_desc_encode_addr(smem_base));
227	    uint64_t lbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((lbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
228	    uint64_t sbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((sbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
229	    uint64_t bo   = static_cast<uint64_t>(base_offset & 0x7u);
230	    uint64_t sw   = static_cast<uint64_t>(Swizzle & 0x3u);
231	    d.desc = (addr)                 // bits 13:0
232	           | (lbo << 16)            // bits 29:16
233	           | (sbo << 32)            // bits 45:32
234	           | (bo  << 49)            // bits 51:49
235	           | (sw  << 62);           // bits 63:62
236	#else
237	    (void)smem_base; (void)lbo_bytes; (void)sbo_bytes; (void)base_offset;
238	    d.desc = 0;
239	#endif
240	    return d;
241	}

244	//  Canonical descriptor builders for the bf16 K-major (K=16) smem operand
245	//  tiles the model headers stage (DESIGN §4.3: A tile 64×16 bf16, B tile
246	//  N×16 bf16). Major-K means the contraction dimension K is the operand's
247	//  inner GEMM dim and the wgmma reads the standard "TN" product
248	//  D[m,n] = Σ_k A[m,k]·B[n,k] with BOTH operands K-major (TransA=TransB=0).
249	//
250	//  REQUIRED smem layout (the CUTLASS-canonical Major-K INTERLEAVE layout —
251	//  ground truth, NOT a plain row-major block; see the report's "deviation"
252	//  section). For an operand of MN rows × 16 K-cols of bf16, element (mn,k) is
253	//  at the bf16 index:
254	//      idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)
255	//  i.e. the K=16 dim is two stacked 8-wide "core matrices", each an MN×8
256	//  row-major block of 128-bit rows: core-matrix 0 (k 0..7) occupies the first
257	//  MN*8 bf16 (MN*16 bytes), core-matrix 1 (k 8..15) the next MN*16 bytes.
258	//  The staging loops in the model headers / self-test / tile_pipeline MUST
259	//  write the tile in THIS layout (make_desc_* assumes it).
260	//
261	//  Descriptor LBO/SBO for this canonical no-swizzle (INTERLEAVE) layout,
262	//  derived from cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K> and verified against the cute
263	//  Layout_K_INTER_Atom byte offsets (report §"descriptor"):
264	//      SBO (stride byte offset)  = 128                 (8 MN-rows × 16 B/row)
265	//      LBO (leading byte offset) = MN * 16             (one core-matrix block)
266	//  Both are passed in BYTES; make_smem_desc applies the mandated >>4.
267	//  make_smem_desc routes lbo_bytes→leading-offset field (bits 29:16) and
268	//  sbo_bytes→stride-offset field (bits 45:32), matching cute's assignment
269	//  (leading_byte_offset_ = stride_10 = MN*16, stride_byte_offset_ = 128).
270	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
271	
272	// A operand (LHS), shape M×K(=16) bf16 in the canonical Major-K smem layout.
273	// `MN` is the operand's MN extent (= the wgmma M = 64 for the A tile).

275	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_desc_A_kmajor(const void* smem_base) {

277	    const uint32_t sbo = 128u;                 // 8 MN-rows × 16 B/row

291	//  fp32 accumulator fragment for an m64×N output tile.
292	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.3 "Register fragment for .f32 accumulators" (the
293	//  m64nNk16 wgmma writes its output across the 128 warpgroup threads).
294	//
295	//  Fragment layout (the ISA figure, decoded):
296	//    - 128 threads = 4 warps; the M=64 rows are split so that
297	//        warp w  (w in 0..3)  owns rows  [16*w .. 16*w+15],
298	//      and within a warp, lane L owns two row-groups:
299	//        row_hi = 16*w + (L/4)        (rows 0..7 of the warp's block)
300	//        row_lo = row_hi + 8          (rows 8..15)
301	//    - The N columns are held as N/2 fp32 registers per thread, in pairs:
302	//        register pair (2c, 2c+1) holds columns (col_base+0, col_base+1)
303	//        where col_base = (L%4)*2 + 8*(c/2_grouped)...  [the (col%8) + 8*(c>>1)
304	//      grouping of the ISA]. We expose the exact decode via frag_row()/
305	//      frag_col() so the epilogue (and the self-test) maps register i of
306	//      lane L (in warp w) to the (row,col) of the 64×N output it represents.
307	//
308	//  We store N/2 floats. c[2*g + p] is the p-th (p in {0,1}) of register-group
309	//  g (g in [0, N/4) for the "even/odd column pair" grouping). The helpers
310	//  frag_row(lane,i) / frag_col(lane,i) give the global (row,col) so a single
311	//  authoritative decode is shared by the epilogue store AND the gate's
312	//  reference comparison (no chance of a mismatched private decode).
313	// =========================================================================
314	template <int N>
315	struct WgmmaAccum {
316	    static_assert(N % 8 == 0, "wgmma N must be a multiple of 8");
317	    static constexpr int kRegs = N / 2;   // fp32 regs per thread
318	    float c[kRegs];
319	
320	    __device__ __forceinline__ void zero() {
321	        #pragma unroll
322	        for (int i = 0; i < kRegs; ++i) c[i] = 0.0f;
323	    }
324	};

326	// --- Authoritative fragment decode (PTX ISA §<ip>.3, .f32 accumulators) -
327	// For thread `tid_in_wg` in [0,128) and register index `i` in [0, N/2):
328	//   warp = tid_in_wg / 32 ; lane = tid_in_wg % 32.
329	//   The 64 M-rows are partitioned warp-major: rows [16*warp, 16*warp+16).
330	//   lane bits decode within the warp's 16-row × N block as in the ISA figure:
331	//     group g = i / 2 ; sub p = i % 2.
332	//     row = 16*warp + (lane / 4) + 8 * (g % 2 == 0 ? 0 : 0)   -- see below.
333	//
334	// The ISA C-fragment for .m64nNk16.f32 lays out each lane's N/2 elements as
335	// (over the row pair r0=lane/4, r1=r0+8) interleaved column pairs. The precise
336	// closed form, validated by the A=I gate, is:
337	//   group_of_8 = i / 8 ;   within = i % 8
338	//   row = 16*warp + (lane/4) + 8*(within / 4)
339	//   col = (lane%4)*2 + (within % 2) + 8*group_of_8 + ...
340	// To keep ONE source of truth that the gate verifies bit-for-bit, the decode
341	// is implemented below in the exact factored form the ISA figure gives for
342	// the 16x8 sub-blocks the f32 accumulator tiles across N.
343	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_frag_decode(
344	    int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col
345	) {
346	    const int warp = tid_in_wg >> 5;       // 0..3
347	    const int lane = tid_in_wg & 31;       // 0..31
348	    // Each 16x8 output sub-block (one "n8" column slab) contributes 4 regs
349	    // per thread (8 rows split into 2 row-halves × ... ). The ISA's .f32
350	    // fragment for an n8 slab gives, per lane:
351	    //   reg 0 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
352	    //   reg 1 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
353	    //   reg 2 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
354	    //   reg 3 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
355	    // and successive n8 slabs add 8 to the column. With N columns there are
356	    // N/8 slabs × 4 regs = N/2 regs (matches kRegs).
357	    const int slab   = i >> 2;             // which n8 column slab (0..N/8-1)
358	    const int within = i & 3;              // 0..3 within the slab
359	    const int row_half = within >> 1;      // 0 -> rows 0..7, 1 -> rows 8..15
360	    const int col_par  = within & 1;       // 0 or 1 column within the pair
361	    row = 16 * warp + (lane >> 2) + 8 * row_half;
362	    col = (lane & 3) * 2 + col_par + 8 * slab;
363	    (void)N;
364	}

626	    // pre-existing fp32 value, it sets FenceBeforeFirst=false, zeroes/sets the
627	    // accumulator + fences itself, and we still issue k=0 below — but then the
628	    // caller should pass an accumulating first step; for the common fresh-tile

630	    {
631	        auto d = gen(0);
632	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
633	    }
634	    #pragma unroll 1
635	    for (int k = 1; k < k_steps; ++k) {
636	        auto d = gen(k);
637	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
638	    }
639	    wgmma_commit_group();
640	    wgmma_wait_group<0>();

642	    (void)acc; (void)k_steps; (void)gen;
643	#endif

272	__device__ __forceinline__ void tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16(

274	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gB,
275	    float* __restrict__ gD, int k_steps
276	) {
277	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
278	    extern __shared__ char smem_raw[];
279	    // 16B-align the ring arena.
280	    uintptr_t base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(smem_raw);
281	    uintptr_t aligned = (base + 15u) & ~uintptr_t(15u);
282	    TilePipeline<N, Depth> pipe(reinterpret_cast<void*>(aligned));
283	    pipe.init_barriers();
284	    __syncthreads();
285	
286	    const int warpgroup = threadIdx.x / 128;    // 0 = producer, 1 = consumer
287	    const bool is_producer = (warpgroup == 0);
288	
289	    // Register rebalance (DESIGN §4.2): producer few regs, consumer many.
290	    // Guarded by SG_TUNED_*_REGS != 0 (0 disables for portability/debug).
291	#if (SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS != 0) && (SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS != 0)
292	    if (is_producer) warpgroup_reg_dealloc<SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS>();
293	    else             warpgroup_reg_alloc  <SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS>();
294	#endif
295	
296	    if (is_producer) {
297	        // Producer: stage every K-tile in ascending k. With Depth buffering it
298	        // may run up to Depth stages ahead; we gate reuse of a slot on the
299	        // consumer having released it (empty[slot]).
300	        unsigned empty_parity[Depth];
301	        #pragma unroll
302	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) empty_parity[s] = 0u;
303	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
304	            const int slot = k % Depth;
305	            // For k >= Depth, the slot was used by k-Depth; wait until the
306	            // consumer released it (empty barrier) before overwriting.
307	            if (k >= Depth) {
308	                pipe.empty(slot).wait(empty_parity[slot]);
309	                empty_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
310	            }
311	            pipeline_produce_ktile<N, Depth>(pipe, slot, k, gA, gB, k_steps);
312	        }
313	    } else {
314	        // Consumer: wgmma over each staged K-tile in ascending k. The fp32
315	        // fragment accumulates across the whole chain (first k overwrites).
316	        WgmmaAccum<N> acc;
317	        unsigned full_parity[Depth];
318	        #pragma unroll
319	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) full_parity[s] = 0u;
320	
321	        // We can't use the kchain helper directly (it expects all descriptors
322	        // available); instead we inline the SAME choreography: one fence, then
323	        // k=0 overwrite / k>0 accumulate, commit+wait at the end. Issuing each
324	        // wgmma right after its stage is ready overlaps load and compute.
325	        wgmma_fence();
326	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
327	            const int slot = k % Depth;
328	            pipe.full(slot).wait(full_parity[slot]);
329	            full_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
330	
331	            __nv_bfloat16* aTile = pipe.stageA(slot);
332	            __nv_bfloat16* bTile = pipe.stageB(slot);
333	            SmemDesc dA = make_desc_A_kmajor</*M=*/64, kSwizzleNone>(aTile);
334	            SmemDesc dB = make_desc_B_kmajor</*N=*/N,  kSwizzleNone>(bTile);
335	            // Both operands Major-K ⇒ TransA=0, TransB=0 (cute Major::K == 0).
336	            if (k == 0) {
337	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
338	            } else {
339	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
340	            }
341	            // Commit + wait THIS issue before releasing the slot, so the
342	            // producer does not overwrite operands the async wgmma still reads.
343	            wgmma_commit_group();
344	            wgmma_wait_group<0>();
345	            // Release the slot back to the producer. ALL 128 consumer threads
346	            // arrive (barrier count=128) — see init_barriers: the per-warp elect
347	            // would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock.
348	            pipe.empty(slot).arrive();
349	        }
350	
351	        // Epilogue: store the fp32 fragment. The consumer warpgroup owns the
352	        // output; decode relative to its 128-thread group (tid-128).
353	        const int tid_in_wg = threadIdx.x - 128;
354	        #pragma unroll
355	        for (int i = 0; i < WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {
356	            int row, col;
357	            wgmma_frag_decode(tid_in_wg, i, N, row, col);
358	            gD[row * N + col] = acc.c[i];
359	        }
360	    }
361	#else
362	    (void)gA; (void)gB; (void)gD; (void)k_steps;
363	#endif

# CuTe device-atom GEMM swap — exhaustive seam map

Goal: replace the hand-rolled ss-wgmma engine (`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/wgmma.cuh`)
inside the persistent megakernel with a CuTe **device-side-atom** GEMM
(`cute::SM90::GMMA::MMA_64xNx16_F32BF16BF16_SS` + CuTe smem swizzle layouts +
`cutlass::PipelineTmaAsync` choreography) that stays device-callable BETWEEN the
hand-built grid barriers. CANNOT use a host-launched `CollectiveMma`. CPU-only audit.

Repo: `/workspace/SuperGrok1.5`. CUTLASS/CuTe v3.6.0 at `third_party/cutlass`.

================================================================================
## 0. THE SEAM IN ONE SENTENCE
================================================================================
Every model stage calls **exactly five `sg::sm90::wgs::` symbols** from `wgmma.cuh`:
`WgmmaAccum<N>`, `make_desc_A_kmajor<MN>`, `make_desc_B_kmajor<MN>`,
`wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N,ScaleD,TransA,TransB>`, plus the choreography trio
`wgmma_fence()/wgmma_commit_group()/wgmma_wait_group<N>()` and the epilogue decode
`wgmma_frag_decode(tid_in_wg,i,N,&row,&col)`. The CuTe swap is **purely internal to
these symbols** — if their ABI (below) is preserved, NO model-stage / megakernel /
launcher line changes. The hand-rolled cp.async ring in `tile_pipeline.cuh` is NOT
used by the production path (see §5); the megakernel inlines its OWN ring inside
`tc_gemm_block_unpipelined` (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:688`).

================================================================================
## 1. THE WGMMA ISSUE PATH (what CuTe replaces) — wgmma.cuh
================================================================================

### 1a. The accumulator fragment — REPLACE WITH CuTe but keep the ABI
`WgmmaAccum<N>` (wgmma.cuh:314-324): `static constexpr int kRegs = N/2; float c[kRegs];`
plus `.zero()`. The 128 warpgroup threads together hold the 64×N fp32 tile; each
thread owns `N/2` regs.
- CuTe equivalent: the accumulator produced by `partition_fragment_C(tiled_mma, ...)`
  / `make_fragment_C` is a `cute::Tensor` of `N/2` fp32 regs with the SAME PTX
  §<ip>.3 thread→(row,col) mapping. **Bit-layout identical** — the closed form in
  `wgmma_frag_decode` (wgmma.cuh:343-364) IS the CuTe C-fragment layout (row =
  `16*warp + lane/4 + 8*(within>>1)`, col = `(lane&3)*2 + (within&1) + 8*(i>>2)`).
- CONSTRAINT: callers index `acc[ai].c[i]` directly (e.g.
  `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1100`, `model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:488`) and the epilogue
  pairs `c[i]` with `wgmma_frag_decode(...,i,...)`. The replacement MUST expose `.c[i]`
  in the SAME order as the decode, or also replace `wgmma_frag_decode`. Simplest: keep
  `WgmmaAccum<N>` as the storage POD, fill it from the CuTe atom's fma outputs.

### 1b. The descriptor builders — REPLACE WITH cute::make_gmma_desc / GmmaDescriptor
- `struct SmemDesc { uint64_t desc; }` (wgmma.cuh:212-214).
- `make_smem_desc<Swizzle>(smem_base, lbo_bytes, sbo_bytes, base_offset)`
  (wgmma.cuh:219-241): packs the PTX §<ip>.4 64-bit descriptor by hand:
    `addr=(__cvta_generic_to_shared(p)&0x3FFFF)>>4` → bits 13:0
    `lbo>>4` → bits 29:16 ; `sbo>>4` → bits 45:32 ; `base_offset` → 51:49 ;
    `Swizzle` → 63:62.
- `make_desc_A_kmajor<MN,Swizzle>(smem)` (wgmma.cuh:274-279) and
  `make_desc_B_kmajor<MN,Swizzle>(smem)` (wgmma.cuh:283-288): both hard-fix
    `lbo = MN*16` (one core-matrix block, bytes), `sbo = 128` (8 rows × 16 B),
    `Swizzle = kSwizzleNone` at every production call site.
- CuTe equivalent: `cute::GmmaDescriptor` union (mma_sm90_desc.hpp:85-160) +
  `cute::make_gmma_desc<GMMA::Major::K>(smem_tensor)` (in mma_traits_sm90_gmma.hpp).
  The hand-rolled `SmemDesc.desc` is **bit-for-bit** a `GmmaDescriptor.desc_`:
  the comment block (wgmma.cuh:243-269) literally cites
  `cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K>` and the `Layout_K_INTER_Atom` byte offsets it
  reverse-engineered (`leading_byte_offset_=MN*16`, `stride_byte_offset_=128`,
  `layout_type_=INTERLEAVE=0`). CuTe's enum (mma_sm90_desc.hpp:53-57):
  `INTERLEAVE=0, B128=1, B64=2, B32=3` — matches `SwizzleMode` (wgmma.cuh:167-172) EXACTLY.

### 1c. The choreography — REPLACE WITH cute warpgroup_* (mma_sm90_gmma.hpp)
- `wgmma_fence()` → `wgmma.fence.sync.aligned` (wgmma.cuh:374-378) ≡
  `cute::warpgroup_fence_operand(reg)` / the fence inside the atom (mma_sm90_gmma.hpp:49,88-99).
- `wgmma_commit_group()` → `wgmma.commit_group.sync.aligned` (wgmma.cuh:385-389) ≡
  `cute::warpgroup_commit_batch()` (mma_sm90_gmma.hpp:76).
- `wgmma_wait_group<N>()` → `wgmma.wait_group.sync.aligned N` (wgmma.cuh:398-403) ≡
  `cute::warpgroup_wait<N>()` (mma_sm90_gmma.hpp:62).

### 1d. The per-N issue overloads — REPLACE WITH the CuTe atom fma
`wgmma_issue_n{8,16,32,64,96,128}<ScaleD,TransA,TransB>(acc, descA, descB)`
(wgmma.cuh:441-561) are hand-written `asm volatile("wgmma.mma_async...m64nNk16.f32.bf16.bf16 {N/2 +f regs}, descA, descB, ScaleD, 1, 1, TransA, TransB")`.
Dispatched by `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N,ScaleD,TransA,TransB>` (wgmma.cuh:573-591) with a
`static_assert(N∈{8,16,32,64,96,128})`.
- CuTe atom: `cute::SM90::GMMA::MMA_64x128x16_F32BF16BF16_SS<Major::K,Major::K>::fma(
  desc_a, desc_b, d00,d01,...,dNN, GMMA::ScaleOut::Zero|One)`
  (mma_sm90_gmma.hpp:2808-2889; alias `cute::SM90_64x128x16_F32BF16BF16_SS` at
  mma_traits_sm90_gmma.hpp:1727). ALL N the engine uses exist as CuTe structs:
  `MMA_64x{8,16,32,64,96,128}x16_F32BF16BF16_SS` (mma_sm90_gmma.hpp:2247-2889) plus
  ext N {24,40,48,56,72,80,88,104,112,120,…} (mma_sm90_gmma_ext.hpp).
- KEY MAPPING: hand-rolled `ScaleD` immediate (0=overwrite/1=accumulate) ↔ CuTe
  `GMMA::ScaleOut::{Zero,One}` (the `scale_D` arg, mma_sm90_gmma.hpp:2834). Hand-rolled
  `scaleA=scaleB=1` (hard-fixed, no operand negate) ↔ CuTe `GMMA::ScaleIn::One`
  template defaults. Hand-rolled `TransA=TransB=0` (production, see §3) ↔ CuTe
  `GMMA::Major::K, GMMA::Major::K` template args.

### 1e. The mainloop helper (a convenience, NOT on the production path)
`wgmma_mainloop_kchain<N,TransA,TransB,FenceBeforeFirst>(acc,k_steps,gen)`
(wgmma.cuh:617-644): one fence, k=0 ScaleD=0, k>0 ScaleD=1, commit + wait_group<0>.
Used ONLY by the substrate selftest, NOT by the megakernel (which inlines the
identical sequence — see §4). The CuTe swap can keep or drop this; the production seam
is the per-issue `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16` call, not the kchain.

================================================================================
## 2. THE SMEM OPERAND LAYOUT (the cute Major-K INTERLEAVE idx)
================================================================================
The canonical layout that `make_desc_*_kmajor` ASSUMES (wgmma.cuh:250-269; the staging
contract):
    idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)            // bf16 element index
i.e. K=16 is two stacked 8-wide core matrices, each an MN×8 row-major block of
128-bit rows: core-matrix 0 (k 0..7) at `mn*8`, core-matrix 1 (k 8..15) at `MN*8+mn*8`.
- The producer-side stager that WRITES this layout: `stage_kmajor_tile<MN,Src>`
  (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:571-582):
    `dst = (k>>3)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k&7); smem_tile[dst] = src(mn, kbase+k);`
- The cp.async half-row form (same map): `half*(MN*8) + mn*8`, 8 bf16 (16 B) per chunk
  (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:838-841 for A, :846-847 for B; mirror in
  `tile_pipeline.cuh:226-239`).
- CuTe equivalent: `cute::GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom<bfloat16>`
  (mma_traits_sm90_gmma.hpp:81,98 — `Swizzle<0,4,3> ∘ Layout<Shape<_8,_128>,Stride<_128,_1>>`
  upcast to bf16) tiled to `Shape<_MN,_16>` via `tile_to_shape`. The hand-rolled idx IS
  this layout's offset function. SWITCHING TO A SWIZZLED LAYOUT
  (`Layout_K_SW128_Atom`, mma_traits_sm90_gmma.hpp:84,104, `layout_type_=B128=1`) is the
  intended perf lever (wgmma.cuh:156-165 flags NONE as the correctness-path layout and
  128B-swizzle as the perf target) — BUT it changes BOTH the descriptor `layout_type_`
  AND the staging write offsets together, so it must be done atomically with the stager.
- SMEM TILE STRIDES (decoder): `kDecTcSmemA1 = 64*16` bf16 (A tile),
  `kDecTcSmemB1 = TILE_N*16` bf16 (B tile) (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:271-272).
  Ring slot layout: A-tiles packed `[slot][atom-in-group]` at
  `sA + (s*kDecAtomsPerSlot + ai)*64*16`, B at `sB + s*N*16`
  (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:356-387; `DecTcSmem.sA/sB` alignas(16)).
- 16-BYTE ALIGNMENT is mandatory (descriptor drops low 4 addr bits, wgmma.cuh:103-108);
  `DecTcSmem.sA` is alignas(16) (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:386,490-492) and every tile
  offset is a multiple of 8 bf16. A CuTe smem tensor over the same `__nv_bfloat16*` arena
  satisfies this; `cute::make_tensor(make_smem_ptr(sA), Layout_K_INTER_Atom...)` is a
  drop-in.

================================================================================
## 3. ORIENTATION (TransA/TransB) — production is ALWAYS K-major/K-major (0,0)
================================================================================
EVERY production wgmma issue uses `<N, ScaleD, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>`:
- decoder: model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:759-760 (issue_k lambda).
- vit:     model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:470-472.
- (tile_pipeline.cuh:337-339 also uses 0,0 — but tile_pipeline is not the prod path.)
The staging lambdas do the PHYSICAL transpose (fwd reads X[m,k]/W[n,k]; dX reads
dY[m,k] + W^T cache; dW reads dY^T/X^T), so the WGMMA always sees Major-K/Major-K
(model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:563-567 "the staging loop transposes physically; the engine
never leaves the gated path"). => CuTe atom template args are fixed
`GMMA::Major::K, GMMA::Major::K` for the whole megakernel; transpose lives in the TMA/
stager, NOT the MMA. This is the single most important invariant for keeping the swap local.

================================================================================
## 4. THE CALL SITES (the ABI the swap must preserve) — central GEMM driver
================================================================================
The engine is `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<N,MaxAtomsM,SrcA,SrcB,Out>(mbase0, m_atoms,
n_real, k_steps, srcA, srcB, out, smemA, smemB, pipeBars=nullptr, prof_phase=-1)`
(model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:687-1130). It is THE one place all wgmma issues happen for
the decoder. Structure:
1. `constexpr int kIL = min(MaxAtomsM, kDecMaxIL)` (=2 prod); `WgmmaAccum<N> acc[kIL]`
   (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:726-727).
2. `issue_k(g_atoms,k,rs)` lambda (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:750-762): builds
   `dB=make_desc_B_kmajor<N>(smemB+sl*kDecTcSmemB1)`, loops ai: `dA=make_desc_A_kmajor<64>(
   smemA+(sl*kIL+ai)*kDecTcSmemA1)`, `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N,k==0?0:1,0,0>(acc[ai],dA,dB)`.
3. Ring branches (all preserve ascending-k / per-k commit+wait_group<0>):
   - `kRingAsync` (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:784-785) = both srcs are
     `DecGmemTileSrc{A,B}` (the flat-gmem K-major trait, :635-637) AND S>1.
   - PIPE=2 producer/consumer mbarrier engine (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:860-987):

     `wgs::fence_async_proxy()`, `decprim::cp_async_*`. **WG split: WG0=consumer(wgmma),
     WG1=producer(cp.async).** BAKED OFF in prod (PIPE=1 won, :186).
   - PIPE=1 deeper cp.async ring RS≤2 (:988-1016) and RS=3..4 (:1017-1062). **BAKED
     DEFAULT** (SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_PIPE=1, STAGES=4, :186-189).
   - non-ring synchronous (dW path, :1063-1085): `stage_k` + `__syncthreads` + fence.
4. Epilogue (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1090-1104): `in_wg0` decodes
   `wgmma_frag_decode(tid_wg,i,N,&row,&col)` and emits `out(mbase+row, col, acc[ai].c[i])`
   for `col < n_real`.

THIN ORIENTATION WRAPPERS (the public ABI the megakernel driver calls;
model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1159-1271) — these define `SrcA/SrcB/Out` and call the engine:
- `dectc_gemm_fwd<N>(X,W,Yout,Kin,Nout,sA,sB,pipeBars)` — Y=X·Wᵀ, both K-major gmem
  (`DecGmemTileSrcA{X,Kin}`, `DecGmemTileSrcB{W+n0*Kin,Kin,Nout-n0}`), :1159-1179.

- `dectc_gemm_dx_f32<N>(dY,WT,dXf32,Kin,Nout,...)` — dX=dY·W from the W^T cache,
  K-contiguous, :1210-1224.

  same engine with `mbase0=mbase`, `MaxAtomsM=kDecDwIL`; lambda OR `DecGmemTileSrc`
  sources (contiguous-transpose stage, :2216-2218).

VIT/MAMBA seam = identical (`make_desc_{A,B}_kmajor<...,kSwizzleNone>` +
`wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N,ScaleD,0,0>` + `wgmma_fence/commit/wait_group<0>` +
`wgmma_frag_decode`): vit model_stage_vit_tc.cuh:444-489; mamba model_stage_mamba_tc.cuh.

ABI THE SWAP MUST KEEP (so the change is local to wgmma.cuh):
- `WgmmaAccum<N>` POD with `.c[i]` (i∈[0,N/2)) ordered to match `wgmma_frag_decode`.
- `SmemDesc make_desc_A_kmajor<MN,Sw>(const void*)`, `make_desc_B_kmajor<MN,Sw>(const void*)`.
- `wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N,ScaleD,TransA,TransB>(WgmmaAccum<N>&, SmemDesc, SmemDesc)`.
- `wgmma_fence()`, `wgmma_commit_group()`, `wgmma_wait_group<N>()`.
- `wgmma_frag_decode(int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col)`.
- N set actually used: 128 (default), plus 96 (decoder head pad), 64 (ragged) and the
  ladder {8,16,32} for the selftest (wgmma.cuh:578-587). All exist as CuTe atoms.

================================================================================
## 5. THE cp.async RING (TilePipeline) — and why the megakernel does NOT use it
================================================================================
`tile_pipeline.cuh`:
- `TileGeom<N>` (tile_pipeline.cuh:104-115): A=64*16 bf16, B=N*16 bf16, row strides 32 B.
- `TilePipeline<N,Depth>` (tile_pipeline.cuh:142-189): `ring` (Depth×(A|B) tiles) +

  for ALL Depth (count=128 = full warpgroup, NOT count-1 — the deadlock fix note,
  tile_pipeline.cuh:173-179).
- `pipeline_produce_ktile<N,Depth>` (tile_pipeline.cuh:206-259): 16B cp.async into the
  canonical interleave, `cp_async_commit/wait_group<0>`, `fence_async_proxy()`,
  `full(slot).arrive()`.

  blockDim=256, WG0=producer / WG1=consumer GEMM. **Used ONLY by the selftest**
  (wgmma_selftest.cu:139). The megakernel re-implements the SAME mbarrier choreography
  INLINE inside `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined` PIPE=2 (the transcription note,
  model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:861-987), NOT by calling `tc_pipelined_gemm`.
- The reused primitives live in `primitives.cuh`: `cp_async_cg_16` (primitives.cuh:497-508),
  `cp_async_commit` (:526-531), `cp_async_wait_group<N>` (:536-542) — these are the
  cp.async ring the prod path's `decprim::cp_async_*` calls bind to.
- `warp_specialize.cuh`: `Mbarrier` (warp_specialize.cuh:72-138: init/arrive/
  arrive_expect_tx/try_wait/wait), `fence_async_proxy()` (:143-147),
  `warpgroup_reg_alloc<N>/dealloc<N>` (setmaxnreg, :159-171), `elect_one_sync` (:41-57).

CuTe-pipeline mapping (for the TMA path the goal asks for):
- `wgs::Mbarrier` ≡ `cutlass::arch::ClusterTransactionBarrier` (barrier.h:512-526:
  `arrive_and_expect_tx(bytes)`) — the byte-counting variant the hand-rolled code
  deliberately AVOIDED (tile_pipeline.cuh:242-255 uses plain arrive + cp_async_wait_group
  because cp.async doesn't auto-count; **TMA DOES auto-count**, so the CuTe path can use
  the real expect_tx).
- The full producer/consumer ring ≡ `cutlass::PipelineTmaAsync` (sm90_pipeline.hpp:271,
  `producer_acquire`/`producer_commit`/`consumer_wait`/`consumer_release` + `PipelineState`
  :171). The hand-rolled full[]/empty[] parity ring is exactly a 2-barrier-per-stage
  PipelineTmaAsync. This is device-constructible (no host launch) → compatible with the
  persistent megakernel.
- setmaxnreg split (`warpgroup_reg_{alloc,dealloc}`) ≡ CuTe `cutlass::arch::warpgroup_reg_
  {alloc,dealloc}`. Prod producer/consumer regs: SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS=40 / CONS_REGS=232
  (tile_pipeline.cuh:92-97).

================================================================================
## 6. HARD CONSTRAINTS THAT GATE THE DESIGN
================================================================================
### 6a. 1-CTA/SM persistent + GridBarrier (NO cooperative launch)
- `GridBarrier` (megakernel_common.cuh:147-255): hand-built sense-reversing
  arrive/wait over global `g_arrived`/`g_generation`; `sync()` (:157-210),
  `sync_reset(int*)` (:222-254). Two `__threadfence()` per CTA (release before
  atomicAdd, acquire after generation advance). Needs NO cooperative launch
  (megakernel_common.cuh:28-29) → scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap.
- The GEMM runs BETWEEN `bar.sync()` calls (e.g. Muon NS matmuls,
  fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1289-1320; dW splitk + bar.sync,
  fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:1075-1081). The CuTe GEMM is invoked the same way —
  device-callable, no kernel relaunch.
- Launch: `__global__ __launch_bounds__(SG_TC_MEGA_BLOCK) fused_decoder_megakernel_tc`
  (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:673-678); `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor`
  REFUSES `occ < 1` (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:310-321 → `cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources`).
  blockDim = 256 (SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK), one persistent CTA per SM (gridDim.x == #SMs,
  megakernel_common.cuh:59,268). **=> ANY CuTe smem growth must keep occupancy ≥ 1.**
  DecTcSmem ≤ 48 KB static cap (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:479-485) or dynamic-smem
  opt-in via `cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` when STAGES>2
  (fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:464-468,679-692).

### 6b. THE TMA BLOCKER (critical) — CUtensorMap is HOST-only in CuTe v3.6.0
- The ONLY descriptor-creation path in CuTe v3.6.0 is `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`, called
  from `make_tma_copy` which is a HOST driver call (copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1008,1268).
  CuTe v3.6.0 has NO device-side tensormap encode (no `tma_descriptor_replace` /
  device `cp_async_bulk_tensor` map-build helper found in copy_sm90_tma.hpp).
- IMPLICATION: a TMA `SM90_TMA_LOAD` needs a `CUtensorMap` built ON THE HOST and passed
  into the kernel as a `const __grid_constant__ CUtensorMap` arg. The persistent
  megakernel takes its tensors as raw `float*`/`DecoderTokenCtx` (fused_decoder_
  megakernel.cuh:674-678) and the operands (acts buffer, C1/C1-T weight cache) are
  CARVED FROM THE WORKSPACE AT RUNTIME (dec_acts_bind / dec_wbf_bind,
  model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:419-438,506-524) — their addresses are not known host-side
  at launch in a fixed way per GEMM. So a full TMA path requires EITHER (i) building the
  tensor maps host-side once per step (the acts/weight-cache base ptrs ARE stable within
  a step → feasible: pass an array of `CUtensorMap` for the ~8 weight matrices + acts
  regions as grid-constant args), OR (ii) keeping cp.async staging and using CuTe ONLY
  for the MMA+descriptor+swizzle (the LOW-RISK swap). RECOMMENDATION: do (ii) first
  (MMA-atom + GmmaDescriptor + swizzled smem layout, reusing the existing cp.async ring),
  then layer TMA via grid-constant tensor maps as a second step.

### 6c. Ascending-k fp32 reduction order (A/A/A bit-determinism)
- The determinism rule: ONE CTA owns the tile end-to-end, k ASCENDING (k=0 ScaleD=0
